Pair with the paper's Section 3 for the generation-execution-optimization architecture.

evolver.what: EvolveR — self-evolving LLM agents via an experience-driven lifecycle: rollout trajectories are distilled into guiding/cautionary principles in a Milvus experience DB, retrieved at task time via a <search_experience> action, and outcome scores reinforce a GRPO-trained Qwen2.5-3B policy (arXiv 2510.16079, ICML 2026).
architecture: evolver/experience/experience_manager.py — ExperienceManager.reflection() runs every training step (experience.organize_interval=1): it flushes the trajectory buffer to the VDB, re-scores each retrieved principle with Laplace-smoothed success (success_count+1)/(usage_count+2) in _update_metric_scores(), then _distill_new_experiences() summarizes each trajectory via SUMMARIZE_SUCCESSFUL/FAILED_TRAJECTORY_PROMPT into a [DESCRIPTION] sentence plus [STRUCTURE] (subject, predicate, object) triplets — typed 'guiding' on success, 'cautionary' on failure — dedups candidates with pairwise MATCH_PRINCIPLE_PROMPT yes/no LLM votes over connected components, then merges into an existing principle (embedding-similarity gate + LLM match, linking the source trajectory as a positive/negative example) or creates a new one; principles scoring under clean_low_metric_threshold=0.3 are purged, as are 'collapsed' ('!!!!!') and special-token-contaminated ones caught at retrieval time.

evolver/experience/milvusdb/ — the 'Experience VDB': a FastAPI server (routers/principles.py, trajectories.py, search.py, export_import.py; start_server.sh) over a single-file Milvus DB; scripts/train_grpo-3b.sh installs a trap that POSTs /export/ of the principles+trajectories collections to data/evolver/result/<experiment>/db_exports as jsonl on exit, and scripts/test-3b.sh restores a prior run via VDB_IMPORT_DB_FILE — the evolved memory is a checkpointable, transferable artifact, not transient context.

evolver/llm_agent/generation.py — the multi-turn rollout (max_turns=10) over <think>/<search>/<search_experience>/<answer> actions: a <search_experience> query calls ExperienceManager.retrieve(top_k=3), returning RetrievedExperiencePackage(principle, similarity_score, positive_examples, negative_examples); _build_prompt_with_experience() packs packages into the token budget with priorities 1. principle description + metric_score, 2. structure subgraph, 3. example trajectories; actor state_masking masks the <information>/<experience> observation blocks out of the policy loss.

evolver/rewards/ + vendored verl/ and LLaMA-Factory/ — outcome_reward_fn (exact match for closed QA; weighted F1 + an LLM 'independence/diversity' score for open-ended) drives GRPO via verl.trainer.main_ppo (algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo; default weights format=0.1, outcome=1.0, experience=0); experience_reward_fn can additionally pay merit_score × embedding-similarity for used principles; scripts/cold_start_sft.sh produces the qwen-3b-instruct-cold_start starting checkpoint, and evolver/search/ serves an e5_Flat.index over the wiki-18 corpus (explicit Search-R1 lineage).
advantages: Memory with a trust ledger: every principle carries usage_count/success_count and a smoothed metric_score that decides both survival (purged below 0.3) and retrieval merit — you can watch individual strategies earn and lose the system's trust across training, which prompt-only memory banks (ACE playbooks, Dynamic Cheatsheet) never measure.

Principles are dual-representation and example-grounded: a natural-language description for embedding retrieval plus SPO-triplet structure, each shipping linked successful AND failed trajectories as few-shot evidence at retrieval time — the most concrete artifact in this catalog for studying strategy (not fact) memory.

The lifecycle closes inside the RL loop itself — distill every step, retrieve during rollouts, reinforce from outcomes — rather than wrapping a frozen model; and jsonl export/import lets one experiment's grown memory seed another (VDB_IMPORT_DB_FILE), making memory evolution itself reproducible.

2609.20519.tldr: Runs auto-research loops over the coding-agent harness itself under a token-efficiency objective: 152 proposed mechanisms, four survive — ~45% fewer tokens and ~1/3 lower cost while retaining ~94% of Pi's score.
2609.20519.method: A 7-stage auto-research loop per candidate idea: Trajectory Rollouts -> Map-Reduce Analysis -> Proposal -> Implementation -> Reviewer -> In-Trajectory Validation -> Held-Out Validation on a frozen, isolated test set. A predeclared capability floor gates every mechanism (savings only count within a quality tolerance, so efficiency is bounded by non-regression), and the surviving mechanisms combine into the SoL-Pi harness.
results: 44.7-49% fewer recorded tokens and ~1/3 lower API cost vs Pi, retaining ~94% of Pi's EdgeBench score (and exceeding the native Codex harness on GPT-5.6 Sol).

Four reusable mechanisms: Action Fusion (fuse edit+run into one call), Online Context Compact (compact at subtask boundaries), ObservationPack (paged recall instead of full replay), Evidence-Preserving Reducer (delegate first reading to a cheaper agent, verify against the log).
In a 20-worker swarm, SoL-Pi workers reach 1,127 cycles at $60.11 — 17.5% fewer cycles and 26.8% lower cost than Pi workers.
limitations: Efficiency measured against Pi and model-native harnesses on EdgeBench/Terminal-Bench; cross-harness transferability is claimed via held-out environments, not yet proven at scale.
Hybrid loop: human priors seeded and filtered the 152-idea pool, so it is not fully autonomous RSI.
The recursive-efficiency compounding ('REI') is explicitly a vision, not a demonstrated effect.
2609.20519.fits: Harness-level RSI with an efficiency objective gated by a capability floor — the non-regression discipline rsif encodes as its val gate, now applied to token cost. Complements rsif (which evolves the agent's artifacts) by evolving the harness that runs the agent.
2609.20519.reading: Read the 7-stage loop and the predeclared capability floor / gate; the four mechanism cards show how narrow harness edits transfer across tasks.

2609.15364.tldr: Training-free recursive self-improvement for brand-new computer environments: curriculum, actor, and verifier agents explore with a broad-then-deep strategy and consolidate verified experience into a memory that is frozen for test-time reuse — lifting open models (GLM-5.3 + Kimi-K3) past GPT-6 Astra on OSWorld 2.0 and Agents' Last Exam.
2609.15364.method: One durable, evolvable memory driven by three coordinated roles: a curriculum agent generates practice tasks from knowledge gaps and decides when practice stops; actor agents execute them code-as-policy and distill their own verified experience back into memory; a verifier agent judges outcomes from environment evidence alone, isolated from the actor's private reasoning to reduce correlated errors. Exploration is broad-then-deep — Broad Recursive Self-exploration (BRS) runs parallel task waves from a shared memory snapshot, consolidated serially per wave with budgets checked at wave boundaries; Deep Recursive Self-exploration (DRS) then does sequential, progressively harder targeted practice, each verified experience committed before the next task is proposed. At test time the memory is frozen and the curriculum agent and memory updates are disabled.
results: OSWorld 2.0 (0808 offline, 82 tasks): partial score 71.97 -> 78.98 and binary accuracy 37.80 -> 42.68 with the same harness and frozen models — above GPT-6 Astra (72.60) and Claude Opus 5 (70.19).
Agents' Last Exam Near-term (67 tasks): 83.75 -> 84.82 partial, 49.25 -> 50.75 binary — above GPT-6 Astra (82.26).

Stage ablation on four OSWorld tasks: full broad+deep 74.54 mean vs 65.52 broad-only and 56.50 deep-only; deep-only from empty memory falls below the baseline on two tasks, so starting focused can hurt.

GameCraft-Bench (40 tasks): improves game quality from both weak and strong base generators, where the Play2Code baseline degrades already-strong games; RSI experience adds further gain on every generator.
limitations: The headline RSI column is not a matched re-run: only 41/82 OSWorld tasks (19/67 ALE) have recorded RSI entries, baseline scores are retained for the rest, and selected retries/checkpoints with differing budgets are included — the repo's PAPER.md documents this aggregation scope.

The acceptance signal is an LLM verifier reading environment evidence, not executed tests; the paper's own failure analysis finds verifier PASS without full requirement coverage and incorrect rules persisting in memory — the failure class rsif moves behind programmatic held-out gates.
Per-environment exploration is expensive (Linux host, Docker/KVM VMs, nominal eight BRS projects per target); gains are demonstrated on two computer-use benchmarks plus one game-development setting.
2609.15364.fits: The closest large-scale cousin of rsif's design: weights frozen, a single artifact (memory) evolves under a trusted outer protocol, verification is separated from acting and isolated from the actor's reasoning, and the result is frozen before evaluation. rsif generalizes the evolving surface (prompt/skill/module/memory/policy/meta), replaces the LLM verifier with executed held-out gates plus canaries, and adds archive/promotion/rollback; RSIAgent shows the pattern surviving at full computer-use scale with open models. Its curriculum actor also mirrors rsif's improver-as-proposal-generator split.
2609.15364.reading: Read Sections 3.2-3.3 for the role split and broad/deep staging, then Section 4.6's failure-mode taxonomy (untargeted exploration, incomplete verification, unreliable memory consolidation) as a checklist for any RSI loop; the repo's docs/ARCHITECTURE.md maps paper stages onto runnable phases (BRS/DRS/test-time reuse).

rsiagent.what: Official implementation of RSIAgent — a training-free multi-agent framework (curriculum, actor, verifier) that recursively explores a new computer environment and consolidates verified experience into a memory that is frozen and reused at test time.
architecture: Three roles: Curriculum Agent (picks practice tasks from knowledge gaps, decides when practice stops), Actor Agent (code-as-policy execution; distills its own verified experience into memory), Verifier Agent (judges outcomes from environment evidence, isolated from the actor's private reasoning and memory).

Three runtime phases: Phase 1 BRS — parallel practice waves from a shared memory snapshot, consolidated serially per wave with budget checks at wave boundaries; Phase 2 DRS — sequential, progressively harder targeted practice, each verified experience committed to memory before the next; Phase 3 — frozen-memory task execution with the curriculum agent and memory updates disabled, followed by sealed official evaluation.

The host harness enforces isolation, records artifacts, commits memory only at valid boundaries (the wave barrier), and keeps benchmark setup and grading outside the learning loop; infra failures stay distinguishable from scored outcomes.
rsiagent.run: Python 3.12 + uv on a Linux host with Docker and /dev/kvm. Clone, `cp .env.example .env` and set OPENROUTER_API_KEY; then per benchmark: pinned OSWorld-V2 v2026.08.08 (tools/prepare_osworld_v2_release.py, smoke_osworld.py) or scripts/setup_ale.py for Agents' Last Exam (~160-170 GiB per OS image). Batches: `python run_osworld.py --arm both --name run_01 --concurrency 1` / `run_ale.py run --arm both`. Credential-free validation: `.venv/bin/python tools/check_rsi_release.py`.
rsiagent.note: The most complete open implementation of explore-verify-remember RSI at computer-use scale. Even without the VM rigs, read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (wave memory barrier, stopping rules, verifier isolation) and docs/PAPER.md (honest aggregation scope of the headline numbers).

2609.24974.tldr: Distills an optimized agent harness into model weights: a harnessing agent reviews and rewrites the student's responses at training time, and SFT on those trajectories moves the behavior into the model — so the specialized harness can be removed at deployment and the gains remain (23.3% → 44.3% macro-average, beating the 41.7% the base model gets with the optimized harness still attached).
2609.24974.method: Three stages. (1) Evolve a student-side harness h* on training tasks, then Adapt it into a private reference harness K for a separate harnessing agent — e.g. a middleware rule that blocks risky actions becomes a review-time warning. (2) Agent-as-harness trajectory collection: the student runs under a fixed minimal target harness h (one bash tool, fixed system prompt); before any response is executed, the harnessing agent reviews it against K and either PASSes it unchanged or REPLACEs it with a complete response valid in h's action space; only the accepted response enters the student-visible trajectory and the review stays private. (3) SFT on the reviewed rollouts (masking reviewer-perspective reasoning), then deploy under h alone.
results: Agent-as-harness beats code-as-harness on frontier models: 81.1% vs 78.1% averaged across six benchmark–model settings.

Harness distillation into Qwen3.5-9B lifts macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3% across SpreadsheetBench / AppWorld / USPTO — above the 41.7% the base model reaches with the evolved harness h* still attached (a 90.1% relative improvement).
82.3% average recovery of 28 harness-induced behavior patterns (memory, skill, tool, middleware) absent from the base model — direct evidence the behavior moved into the weights.
Supervision-source ablation: harness-guided review (30%) far exceeds direct trajectories from a stronger model, trajectories under h*, review without K, or review given only the task answer (3–15%).
limitations: Depends on a capable harnessing model; with weaker models review can become harmful and agent-as-harness loses its edge over code-as-harness.
Reviewing every proposal multiplies collection cost (an extra model call per step; ~2.4× USPTO latency) — though the overhead is absent after distillation.

Some harness mechanisms (notably context management) are not fully expressible as student responses, and SFT may not fully internalize deep domain knowledge — so it narrows rather than removes the need for a harness.
2609.24974.fits: The clearest demonstration yet of the harness→weight transfer rsif's policy surface points at: an optimized harness's induced behaviors are distilled into model parameters via a temporary reviewing agent, then the harness is removed. rsif evolves its artifacts directly under programmatic gates; Harness-Zero shows the complementary move — that harness gains can be converted into training signal and folded back into weights, collapsing a harness collection into one minimal harness. Its agent-as-harness-beats-code-as-harness result is the key empirical claim to weigh against rsif's code-as-substrate stance.
2609.24974.reading: Read §3 for the evolve→adapt→review→SFT pipeline (the PASS/REPLACE review boundary and why the review stays private), then §4.2's agent-as-harness vs code-as-harness comparison and §4.4's supervision-source ablation (30% vs 3–15%) as the tightest evidence for review quality.

harness-zero.what: Official implementation of Harness-Zero — agent harness distillation. architecture: Two harness families per domain under harness_bank/: the evolved student-side h* (tools, middleware, skills, memory in the DeepAgents abstraction) and its adaptation K for the harnessing agent (action recipes, review middleware, review guidance, failure patterns).

Core pipeline in src/harness_zero/: review schema, the harnessing agent, the student wrapper, trajectory store, SFT datum builder, and a Tinker training loop, exposed through a CLI (run-rollout → build-sft → train-sft).
src/deepagents_harbor/ is the Harbor Docker-sandbox backend; AppWorld gets a dedicated env/ (mini-SWE-agent + environment + image build) because its rollouts need a specialized rig.

Clone, `uv sync` (add `--group tinker` for training), copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set the route you use (OpenAI / Azure / OpenRouter / Tinker). Rollout: `harness-zero run-rollout --dataset data/uspto --components harness_bank/uspto --teacher-middleware-factory harness_bank.uspto.middlewares:build_teacher_middlewares ...`, then `build-sft` and `train-sft`.

2609.24972.tldr: Regularizes harness self-improvement so it doesn't overfit the evolve split: proposal-side constraints (annealed edit budget, history-conditioned proposer, exploration redirection) and selection-side constraints (a critic that screens benchmark-specific edits, a noise-adjusted floor, a cost rule, and a pruner) favor reusable mechanisms over benchmark-specific ones — up to +14.1 points in-distribution and up to +4.7 on five held-out benchmarks, while the evolved harness runs on ~30% fewer policy tokens.
2609.24972.method: A harness-evolution loop where the edit space stays open (prompts, control flow, config, context, tools, skills, memory, sub-agents) but the search is regularized. Proposal side: an annealed budget b_t caps how many edits one candidate can bundle; the proposer is conditioned on the full edit history so a falsified hypothesis isn't redrawn; a stalled run is redirected toward components it has never exercised. Selection side: a critic screens every candidate for suite-specific logic before evaluation; a noise-adjusted floor blocks gains within evaluation variance; a cost rule requires added inference tokens to be paid for by measured gain; and components that stop helping are pruned. Each candidate is drafted, screened and evaluated in its own git worktree, and accepting one fast-forwards the branch — the incumbent is always a commit.
results: Coding (Claude Opus 4.8 policy): Terminal-Bench 2.1 +6.0 (74.2 → 80.2) on the evolve split; SWE-bench Verified +1.8 (82.0 → 83.8) out-of-distribution.
Agentic workspace: Harvey LAB +1.1 evolve; JobBench +4.7, GDPval +3.5, APEX-Agents +3.7 out-of-distribution.
Engineering design: EngDesign +4.9 evolve; Frontier-Eng +4.3 out-of-distribution.
Not tied to one policy family: with Gemini 3.5 Flash the coding instance goes 64.6 → 78.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 76.8 → 79.0 on SWE-bench Verified.
The evolved harness runs on ~30% fewer policy tokens than unregularized evolution.
limitations: Regularization narrows but does not close the OOD gap — up to +4.7 points out-of-distribution versus up to +14.1 on the evolve split, so in-distribution overfitting is reduced, not eliminated.
Depends on capable LLM roles (proposer, analyst, critic, selector) and a strong frozen policy (Claude Opus 4.8 / Gemini 3.5 Flash); behavior with weaker models is not demonstrated.
Each instance is a hand-built Domain adapter with per-domain hyperparameters (the noise band is calibrated per instance), so porting to a new domain is engineering work, not automatic.
The critic is an LLM regex-deny + review screen for leakage, not a guarantee of non-leakage; the noise floor is an empirical estimate.
2609.24972.fits: The closest published match to rsif's non-regression discipline, applied at the harness layer. RRSI's noise-adjusted acceptance floor, cost rule, and pruner are the direct analogs of rsif's val gate, budget constraints, and archive promotion/rollback — and its critic is the analog of rsif's held-out gates and canaries, all aimed at the same failure mode rsif engineers against: gains that memorize the training surface instead of generalizing. Where rsif evolves the agent's artifacts under executed gates, RRSI evolves the harness's edit space under measured-score gates.
2609.24972.reading: Read §3 for the proposal- and selection-side constraints (the repo README's method-to-code table maps each rule to its implementation file); Table 6's round-by-round accept/reject case studies are the clearest picture of the regularization actually firing — a candidate rejected by the cost rule, another by the noise floor, a small reusable fix retained.

rrsi.what: Official implementation of RRSI — regularized recursive self-improvement of agent harnesses. A single search core drives three Domain instances (coding, workspace, engineering-design), drafting, screening and evaluating harness candidates in git worktrees and fast-forwarding the branch to each winner.
architecture: One core, three instances: rrsi/ holds the search loop (evaluate, propose, analyst, digester, critic, selection, history, schedule, components); each domains/<name>/ is a Domain adapter (evolve/heldout/smoke splits, run/score, leakage denylist, guards) plus its starting harness and rrsi.json hyperparameters.

Candidates in git worktrees: every candidate harness is drafted, screened and evaluated in its own worktree on a branch off evolve/<domain>; accepting one fast-forwards the branch, so the incumbent is always a commit and the edit history (one JSONL record per edit: component, hypothesis, score/cost change, verdict) is auditable.

Method-to-code is explicit: the annealed budget in schedule.py, history/stall/exploration in history.py, the critic leakage screen in critic.py, the noise-adjusted floor + cost rule in selection.py, and novelty over structural component types in components.py.
rrsi.run: Python 3.10+, plus per-instance environments (harbor for the coding instance; a Python 3.11 env with `pip install -e .[agentic]` for workspace/engineering). Point the roles at a LiteLLM model string (default Claude Opus 4.8 on Vertex AI: set VERTEX_PROJECT / VERTEX_LOCATION). Then `python3 rrsi.py --domain coding baseline` then `run`, `status`; `--T/--k/--delta/--beta1` override rrsi.json, and `readjudicate`/`reevaluate` re-apply a round.
rrsi.note: Read domains/<name>/rrsi.json and the method-to-code table in the README to see each regularization rule as an actual function — especially selection.py (noise-adjusted floor + cost rule) and critic.py (leakage screen), which are the concrete, copyable forms of the discipline rsif encodes as its val gate and held-out gates.
